rules.rule: For short-window crypto price questions, record a spot price from the exchange and pair named in the resolution rules (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT), no more than an hour old at judgment time when the window closes within a day, and state its timestamp and age.

For crypto threshold questions, report the percent distance from current spot to the strike, the hours left in the window, and recent realized volatility over a similar span, noting whether the window falls on a usually quieter weekend.

Read the crypto resolution rules for the exact strike, venue and test (any touch in the window or a close at a set candle), restate that strike at the top of the research, and measure every price fact against it, not against a nearby round number.

Do not treat earlier-week touches of a level or prior days' closes as evidence about the current window; identify what drove those moves (e.g. a weekday bond-yield spike) and check whether that driver is still active now.

For short-horizon crypto questions, search same-day macro and geopolitical news (dollar, bond yields, oil, major policy statements) and report any specific catalyst with timestamps, or state plainly that none was found; label weeks-old news as stale background.

Before reporting a past high or low as reaching the strike, confirm it on the resolution venue's own candles (e.g. Binance 1-minute) and that it falls inside the question's window; label any report naming no exchange, or dated before the window opened, as unverified.
For single-match win questions, read the resolution rules to confirm whether only a win in regulation time counts, and state plainly that a draw would resolve No.

For match questions, report the current-season head-to-head with its game count (under about 10 games is small; note source disagreements) and each side's dated, sourced absences and returns; when injury sources disagree, check the confirmed matchday squad or lineup.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

For tennis 'completed match' questions, read which endings count as not completed (retirement, walkover), and report the historical share of matches finished through normal play at that tour level (WTA 125, ATP Challenger) as the starting reference.

For tennis completion questions, report as risk evidence only specific, dated news from the past week: an injury, a withdrawal, or a retirement at this event; label old retirements, back-to-back events or qualifying load, and a result not yet posted as weak context.

Just before a tennis match, check the tournament's latest order of play, draw updates and withdrawal lists for walkovers, late withdrawals or lucky-loser swaps, and report recent full matches each player finished (singles or doubles) as fitness evidence.

For player-prop questions, confirm every fact names the exact player in the question and discard facts about teammates; report that player's role, usage near the goal line or red zone, and how the opponent defends his position.

For single MLB games, report both confirmed starters' season ERA and ERA+ and recent starts, each team's season record, late-season form (record and offense since Sept 1) and home field; if it is a bullpen game, note that an opener's few innings carry little weight.

For playoff series and games, give the series score, what the trailing team still needs and where, earlier games' margins, current-season records and head-to-head, and whether standing rests on seeding; label past seasons' playoff records as small-sample background.

For in-round golf leader questions, pull the live hole-by-hole leaderboard and, for the named player and everyone within about 3 shots, report score, holes left and tee wave, plus the field's scoring average and how the rules settle a tie for the lead.

For 'next video' view questions, record when the question opened, check the channel's live upload list for any video posted since then, treat it as the resolving video, and report its upload timestamp, hours elapsed in the 168-hour window and current views.

For view-count bracket questions, build reference figures only from first-168-hour counts of the channel's recent comparable uploads; label cumulative or lifetime totals, figures with unclear snapshot dates, and months-old uploads as not the resolution metric.

When a count question resolves on one named data provider, pull that provider's own trailing 2–4 week figures and write down its counting method (e.g. AIS-visible only) first; set aside other trackers' figures that count differently.

Take historical base-rate counts and series streaks only from a cited source covering the current format and running through the latest meeting; label any count recalled from memory, disputed between sources, or built on about a dozen cases as unverified.
